Alex — great to meet you both this morning. Short answers up front, followed by next steps.

Recap / short answers:
- Default: Redwood does capture request metadata and optional request/response bodies for debugging and quality monitoring, but logging of full request/response payloads is configurable per-customer and off by default for sensitive workloads.
- Redaction: we support both ingestion-time masking (configurable regex/PII patterns) and storage-time transformations. Ingestion-time masking is recommended when you want to avoid storing any sensitive fields.
- Headers/trace IDs: you can supply a header-filter list; we also support hashing (HMAC with customer-provided salt) for trace IDs so they remain linkable for tracing without exposing raw IDs.
- Retention/purges: per-customer retention windows are configurable (e.g., 7/30/90/365 days). We support on-demand data purges; standard SLA for purge requests is 7 business days for hosted customers — shorter for Dedicated/Private.

Next steps:
1) Ethan (solutions architect) will send an example redaction config and a short note on the hashing approach.

3) If FintechCo wants a POC, we can spin up a short-term dedicated environment with stricter defaults (no request bodies logged, ingestion-time masking enabled).

Alex / team — following up with a compact example of our redaction and retention options. Notes below and attached sample YAML config (redaction-sample-config.yaml).

Key options (overview):

1) Ingestion-time masking (recommended for PII):
   - pattern-based rules (regex) for common data types: emails, credit-card, SSN, phone numbers.
   - custom named capture rules: you can specify JSON/field paths (e.g., payload.user.ssn) to mask before write.
   - sample rule: maskGroup: true => replaces matching groups with <REDACTED>.

2) Header filtering & trace ID handling:
   - header_allowlist / header_denylist: list headers to keep or drop.
   - trace_id_strategy: ["drop" | "hash" | "preserve"]. Hash uses HMAC-SHA256 with a per-tenant key; hashes are truncated but consistent so traces can be correlated.

3) Storage & encryption:
   - logs are written encrypted at rest (TLS in transit + AES-256 at rest). For Dedicated/Private we can integrate customer KMS/HSM so Redwood never has plaintext keys.

4) Retention & purge:
   - retention_days: integer per-log-type (requests, responses, audit, metrics).
   - purge API: synchronous request to delete data for tenant_id; typical hosted SLA 7 business days, expedited for enterprise contracts.
\5) Option to disable request/response logging entirely and rely on aggregate metrics + sampling.

Example caveats and tradeoffs:
- Ingestion masking is lower risk but can add CPU overhead; for high-throughput workloads we offer optimized native masking kernels.
- Hashing trace IDs preserves traceability without storing raw identifiers, but it is reversible only if your tenant key is compromised (we recommend customer-managed key).

Attachment: redaction-sample-config.yaml (shows masked fields, header_denylist, trace_id_strategy: hash, retention_days mapping).
